m.h:
Cobalt skillchompas can be caught using box traps at the Tree Gnome Stronghold. This area can be accessed by travelling south-west from the Barbarian Outpost or by using the shortcut north of the Grand Tree within the Tree Gnome Stronghold (requiring level 19) Agility.

Once trapped, they become stackable items, so players may hunt them for long periods of time without needing to bank.

This guide assumes 372 skillchompas are caught per hour with an approximate yield of 1.5 per trap. However, the amount caught per trap scales with Agility level; from level 42 Agility, this amount will be from 2 up to 6. At 50 Agility, the average is around 4.1.

m.h:
Crimson skillchompas can be caught using box traps at the Desert Quarry Hunter area, which is found south of the Desert Quarry. As this Hunter area is located in the desert, players should bring waterskins or an enchanted water tiara to avoid taking damage from the desert heat. Wearing desert camouflage gear or graahk hunter gear may increase the success rate in catching crimson skillchompas while hunting in this area. Once trapped, crimson skillchompas become stackable items, so players may hunt them for long periods of time without needing to bank.

This guide assumes 545 skillchompas are caught per hour with an approximate yield of 0.7 per trap. However, the amount caught per trap scales with Agility level; from level 94 Agility, this amount will be from 2 up to 6.

m.h:
Graahks can be found north of Cairn Island, in Karamja, and are easily accessibly via the fairy ring code . They are hunted using a teasing stick and pitfall trapping with logs and a knife.

At level 41 Hunter, the graahks will commonly jump over your pitfall traps, so 60+ Hunter is recommended to reduce the time it takes to capture a graahk. A set of Larupia hunter gear may also improve catch rates.

When captured, graahks will yield either a graahk fur or a tatty graahk fur. The exact ratio of tatty to perfect furs vary with your Hunter level. The latter should be discarded, as it's only worth 91 coins, but the perfect furs are worth 42048 coins.

Green salamanders can be caught using a net trap in the Mort Myre Swamp south-east of Canifis. The hunting spot closest to the Canifis bank is just south-west of the Werewolf Agility Arena. This spot has 4 young trees close together, allowing you to set up 4 traps at once with 60 Hunter, using 4 small fishing nets and 4 ropes. To maximise the amount of lizards you bank per trip, you can leave your traps set up as you run to the bank rather than pick them all up and carry them with you. They will have fallen by the time you get back, so you will have to pick up the ropes and nets and reset the traps. Note: There is a chance the ropes and nets will disappear if you take too long. It is important to stay focused when using this method.

Green salamanders can be difficult to catch at lower levels, therefore it is recommended to use a familiar that invisibly boosts your hunter level, such as a spirit larupia (level 57 Summoning) or an arctic bear (level 71 Summoning).

rq.h: or Hunter's Catalyst fragment or Combined Catalyst fragment

m.h:
Teleport to the Anachronia lodestone and head to the pavosaurus rex location, just south of the feral dinosaurs. You can use Anticipation or Freedom to avoid pavosaurus rex's stuns. Set up your traps, checking and relaying them as grenwalls are caught. With completion of the Medium Tirannwn achievements bait is not required to trap grenwalls. Level 80 Hunter is recommended as it allows five box traps to be placed at the same time. The arctic bear familiar gives an invisible +7 boost to Hunter and scentless flasks give a slight improvement to catch rate.

This guide is based on 200 grenwall catches per hour and an average of 19.5 grenwall spikes per catch. At level 99 Hunter, it's possible to achieve up to 370 catches per hour.

The bonecrusher, seedicide, and herbicide can be used to clean up drops from the grenwalls to conserve inventory space. Wielding the Hunter's Catalyst fragment or Combined Catalyst Fragment will automatically reset the player's box traps when they are triggered but fail to catch a creature. The catalyst fragments require completion of Sliske's Endgame to obtain. If owned, use of the volcanic trapper outfit is highly recommended as it gives a 7% increased success chance, 10% chance of double loot, allows 6 box traps to be placed at once, and gives a 30% chance to instantly deploy/pick up traps. A super hunter or extreme hunter potion could also be used to boost your Hunter level.

To hunt them in the Herblore Habitat the required environment for catching them consists of a blue vine blossom, a lergberry bush, a thermal vent, and an orange tree.

On Anachronia, they can be found near the north-west of the Anachronia base camp, or in the northwest of Anachronia Swamp Fortress in the southeast of the island.

Should you choose to hunt them on Anachronia the required hunter level is 84.

Using scentless potion, trapper outfit and arctic bear familiar, it's possible to achieve over 600 catches per hour at level 99 Hunter.

The seedicide are used to gain XP in Farming, which is not mentioned in XP gains.

Zamorak's favour boosts Hunter experience by 10%, it is optional but very cheap.

If you have Invention unlocked and level 80+ in Hunter, it is highly recommended to wear the trapper outfit, as there is a 10% chance of double loot, so you can maximise your profit, although it does not double marble vine loot.

m.h:
The outputs is approximate.

Puro-Puro is the choice spot to hunt implings as you are guaranteed to see large numbers of them at any given time. The most effective strategy involves snaring the target impling with a Bind spell then catching it while it is rendered immobile. The bind spell can only be cast when next to the target unless you are wielding a mainhand magic weapon. This will require you to swap to a staff/wand to snare then back to your net to catch the impling. To keep the rarer implings spawning, be sure to catch all implings that are higher-level than nature implings, including nature implings themselves.

Expect for the majority of the implings you see to be nature implings; magpies and zombies are approximately the same rarity; ninjas and pirates are significantly rarer. Dragon and Kingly implings are the rarest (thus the most valuable) appearing about 1 - 2 times an hour; it is possible to see more than 2 or none at all with no guarantees on appearances.

Wielding a magic butterfly net increases the catch rate on implings by 15%. As it is considered a magic weapon, it can be used to cast spells. Implings can only be bound by spells from the normal spellbook; ice does not work. Entangle, a level 79 spell, requires 3 nature runes to bind the target for 24 seconds.

Prior to catching implings, have enough impling jars on hand to stock at Elnock Inquisitor and buy the Imp repellent and jar generator. The repellent can be bought for three young, two gourmet and one earth impling jar. The jar generator can be bought for three essence, two eclectic and one nature impling jar. The jar generator can generate up to 33 impling jars per item; destroy it on the last charge. When it reaches 18 charges, immediately hunt the implings needed to rebuy it again.

It is also encouraged to enter from a Gielinor crop circle to gain the Farmer's affinity boost, which will significantly speed up powering through the wheat fields. The boost lasts for 30 minutes of in-game time.

m.h:
Sabre-toothed kyatt are found at the northern part of the Rellekka Hunter area. Create a pitfall trap by using one set of logs from a nearby dead tree with a knife on your tool belt. Click on one of the kyatt to tease them, which makes them attack and follow you around. Walk over to your set up pitfall trap with the kyatt right behind you and jump over it. The kyatt will either walk over it and fall in, or it will jump over as well. If it jumps over, set up a new trap at a new spot (they won't go over the same pitfall trap twice in a row) and repeat the process until the kyatt falls in. Collect a pair of big bones and either tatty kyatt fur or kyatt fur. If you get tatty fur, drop it and bury the bones, then continue to collect the non-tatty fur to sell on the Grand Exchange.

The quickest way to bank is with a charged TokKul-Zo to the Fight Caves, if you have completed The Elder Kiln. After banking at the Fight Caves, use the fairy ring to teleport south of the Feldip Hunter area. Run off the mountain then to the north over a small strip of land. Continue north until you reach the hunting area.

It is recommended to use the tree pitfall traps to the west on the non-snowy part of the hunter area. The kyatt spawn close to the traps and have a smaller walking range than those to the east. With a high Hunter level, you can continually catch the same kyatt right after it spawns if it never jumps over your traps.

Summoning familiars such as the spirit larupia, spirit graahk, and spirit kyatt (level 57 Summoning) or the arctic bear (level 71 Summoning) will invisibly boost your Hunter level, making it less likely that a kyatt will jump over your traps.

m.h:
Spined larupia are found at the southern part of the Feldip Hunter area. Larupia are a consistent moneymaker due to the demand for their furs which are used in the creation of the Larupia outfit and Spirit larupia pouch.

  1. Create a pitfall trap by using one set of logs from a nearby jungle tree with a knife on your tool belt.
  2. Click on one of the larupia to tease them using a teasing stick, which makes them attack and follow you around.
  3. Walk over to your set up pitfall trap with the larupia right behind you and jump over it. The larupia will either walk over it and fall in, or it will jump over as well. If the larupia jumps over, set up a new trap at a new spot (they won't go over the same pitfall trap twice in a row) and repeat the process until the larupia falls in.
  4. Collect a pair of big bones and either tatty larupia fur or larupia fur. If you get tatty fur, drop it and bury the bones, then continue to collect the non-tatty fur to sell on the Grand Exchange.

The quickest way to bank is with a charged TokKul-Zo to the Fight Caves, if you have completed The Elder Kiln. After banking at the Fight Caves, use the fairy ring to teleport north of the Feldip Hunter area, then run south to the larupia hunting grounds.

It is recommended to use the southern-most pitfall trap near the red sandstone mine. One larupia spawns directly south of the southern-most trap, and another spawns directly west of the pitfall trap northwest of the southern one. With a high Hunter level, you can continually catch the same larupia right after it spawns if it never jumps over your traps.

Summoning familiars such as the spirit larupia, spirit graahk, and spirit kyatt (level 57 Summoning) or the arctic bear (level 71 Summoning) will invisibly boost your Hunter level, making it less likely that a larupia will jump over your traps. Alternatively, if you have completed As A First Resort, you can take a dip in the mud bath in Oo'glog to the south for a temporary 10% Hunter boost if you have a Hunter level of at least 48.

m.h:
Orange salamanders are in high demand as they are valuable source of Invention components through disassembly.

Utilizing Sign of the porters or Grace of the Elves as alternative methods to Magic Notepaper reduces input cost, and recommended if players have access through the Divination skill.

Al Kharid Lodestone is not bad for people who want a free teleport out to this hunting location, though it can be quite a run, a Dominion medallion is a much closer teleport. This method is similar to hunting red salamanders. While the profit is lower, the experience may be slightly higher because orange salamanders are faster to catch. The Hunter level requirements are also lower. Unlike the older method, this method does not require banking as regularly as you have Magic notepaper to keep you going.

Small fishing nets and ropes are cheap but might not be always available on the Grand Exchange. Nicholas Angle's Fishing Shop (northeast of Taverley lodestone) and Shantay Pass Shop (south of broomstick teleport after exiting from fountain) are convenient sources of them respectively.

If your goal is Hunter experience this method will be more effective than the older method as using magic notepaper, although more expensive, should allow you to reach up to 400 or so orange salamanders caught per hour, but should still make the same or more profit per hour. This method should be very effective for Hunter experience outside of the Wilderness and not a bad money making method.

Polar kebbit hunting is one of the best money making method for a level 1 hunter until level 29, when one can hunt green salamanders. This method is just as effective at level 1 as at level 99, and only depends on the familiarity of the player with the routes of the kebbit, so it is worth the time to take time to read through this whole guide for tips if you are unfamiliar with hunting Polar kebbits.

About 105 kebbits may be hunted in one hour by using the Hunting Area in Taverley. On banking runs, it is recommended to use the lodestone teleport to save 1 or two seconds on the run from the bank to the hunting area, and also giving you time to rest. Each inventory should consist of 26 Polar kebbit fur as each kill will give 3 drops, meaning you will be forced to drop items to make the kill. Bones should be buried in pairs instead of after every kill as 2 bones can be buried in one animation. The raw beast meat should be dropped while examining one of the rocks to save time as it holds no true monetary value.

To start each route, search one of the 2 burrows ("hole") located at the north and south ends of the hunting area. Tracks will appear, which will lead to set places. Click on a rock close to the end of the tracks that you speculate the next set of track will lead to. Without memorizing every pattern, there are several ways to easily identify/narrow down the rocks the kebbit passes by.

1. The kebbit track will never cross over the original tracks like a + sign. It may overlap, but never crosses over.
2. After the second set of tracks has been found, the next tracks will have to lead to a snow drift, and only the two on the east and western side of the hunting area.
3. The tracks don't double back.
4. The rocks that will have fur on them will always be close to the end of the tracks.

m.h:
Teleport to the Fremennik lodestone and go north and slightly east, through a few aggressive Rock Crabs and a narrow snowy path to arrive at the Rellekka Hunter area to hunt sabre-toothed kebbits. Their teeth can be ground into dust used in Herblore for making Hunter potions. Cut dead trees in the area for logs to set the trap.

This article assumes one trip in 12 minutes (for 28 kebbit teeth each trip; without using a Beast of Burden) or five trips per hour.

As only one deadfall trap can be set at a time, most of the time is spent waiting for a trap to be triggered. Hunting other creatures in the same area (particularly Snowy knight and Sapphire glacialis for high-level players) can greatly increase experience gain. Kebbit teeth dust is worth more than kebbit teeth alone - assume grinding before selling.

Viridian skillchompas can be caught using box traps at the Port Phasmatys Hunter area, which is found south of Port Phasmatys. Once trapped, viridian skillchompas become stackable items, so players may hunt them for long periods of time without needing to bank.

inp.nt: Obtained during method, time and xp factored.

m.h:
Starting from the Memorial to Guthix bank, withdraw at least 2 box traps (4 recommended) and head south towards the Ferret (Hunter) near Nikolaus. Capture 20 ferrets and bank them at the Memorial to Guthix before returning for a second inventory of 20 ferrets. This should take about 7 minutes with 2 box traps, or as little as 6 minutes with 4 traps. Make sure to bank the other 20 ferrets and your box traps. We will be taking 5 ferrets per inventory as "bad luck" protection, but acquiring an inventory of 32 rabbit feet should only take about 3 ferrets on average, so you may have up to 20 extra ferrets once finished.

After acquiring 40 ferrets, withdraw 5 ferrets, 4 rabbit snares, and 1 spirit terrorbird pouch. Head east to the rabbit holes in the Piscatoris Hunter area and summon your spirit terrorbird on the way. Place 4 traps directly east of the westernmost rabbit hole, and then begin spam-clicking the northernmost rabbit hole to "Flush" the hole with a ferret until the 4 rabbit snares are full. This can take anywhere from 4 flushes to 12 depending on which path the rabbits take. Check all 4 snares, and replace them. If you do have a Bonecrusher, drop Raw Rabbit after your snare is visually set up to be able to move one tick earlier while clearing your inventory, otherwise hotkey drop your 4 raw rabbits while moving back to the flushing hole, or while flushing. If you do not have a Bonecrusher, you will additionally have to drop or bury the Bones. After you have collected 12 rabbit feet and you do not have any snares in your inventory, press the button in the familiar window to deposit items into your familiar. As the familiar cannot hold ferrets, only rabbit feet will be taken as long as you do not have undeployed snares, or undropped bones or raw rabbit.

After your inventory and your familiar's inventory are filled, return to the Memorial to Guthix bank to empty your and your familiar's inventory, and withdraw 5 more ferrets and 4 rabbit snares. You should not have lost any rabbit snares, but you should be down between 2 and 4 ferrets on a normal inventory. One inventory of 32 rabbit feet should take about 6 to 7 minutes, including time to bank.

When your summoning points are low, teleport to a small obelisk to refill your summoning points after you have banked, and while you have ferrets and snares. One recommended location is the Tribute stone next to the Falador lodestone due to its low requirements. After that, lodestone teleport to Eagles' Peak and head north to the rabbit holes to continue your trips. Optionally, you can sip doses of Summoning potion while banking to save time.

Including the time to catch ferrets, players can expect about 8-9 inventories of 32 rabbit feet per hour assuming 4 traps, a spirit terrorbird, and Surge are used. The estimate used in the header is for 8, as consistently reaching 9 can be a more intensive task.

The steps for each of the magic weapons are as follows:

  1. Craft eternal magic logs to create an inert form of the chosen weapon.
  2. With rune essence or pure essence, travel to the highest elemental (+2 to progress) or catalytic (+3 to progress) runecrafting altar.
  3. Select the altar's Imbue weapons option.
  4. Repeat the imbuing process until the weapon is in a saturated state. Beware of upgrading to ascended as this will destroy the weapon.

The main profit comes from completing the spider leg or obtaining Araxxi's fang.

  • The Spider leg can be made by combining three of the leg pieces that can be acquired by doing different paths of the boss.
  • At any time, there are 2 out of 3 paths open and available to fight and paths rotate every 4 days.
  • This means the player cannot complete the leg on the same day regardless of the luck that one has in drops.
  • This also means that the player may not make lots of profit instantly. However, if the player keeps killing Araxxi over the course of few days, killing this boss can be one of the best money making methods.

In terms of weapon hilt drops:

  • Araxxi's fang is the most valuable of the three drops and is worth 301634229-202478395 gp each. Fangs are most commonly obtained when fighting Araxxor in its melee form, indicated by red-tipped legs. While this form allows players to kite Araxxor making it easier by reducing damage taken, failing to do so can result in additional bleed damage, potentially increasing the encounter's difficulty at higher enrage levels.
  • Araxxi's eye is worth 251281029-202478395 gp for each drop.
  • Araxxi's web is worth 250944632-202478395 gp for each drop.
  • If the profit from attaching eyes or webs to spider legs falls below 3,000,000 coins, they are best disassembled for their free noxious component.

More information on killing Araxxi can be found in the Araxxor strategy guide.

m.h:
The profit assumes that the player owns all achto gloves, boots, and helmets except one helmet piece, owns the equivalent non-achto helmet and does not reroll the loot. Your profit may be higher or lower depending on these factors.

Due to this boss requiring a large number of players, it may be difficult or time consuming to find a reliable team. Kill times can range from 3-6 minutes. This guide assumes 5 kills per hour by default.

For strategies regarding the fight see this strategy guide.

Strategy for most profitable looting:

  • 5000 reputation will grant the player a 10% drop chance increase
    • If no achto piece or codex is obtained, it is recommended to reroll.
  • Different achto pieces are worth different amounts of gold. A helmet piece like Achto Teralith helmet is worth the most at 8,400,000 gp as it converts to that amount of gold when lost in the wilderness. Gloves and boots are worth 6,000,000 gp.
    • Beastmaster Durzag only drops helmets, gloves, and boots.
    • Using the High Alchemy spell on Achto Teralith helmet will only convert it to 4,200,000 gp and can be used on ironman accounts.
    • To obtain helmets, the player must own all boots and gloves of all achto equipment.
      • Achto equipment is dropped in a specific order.
    • The drop chance of achto can be doubled by owning the equivalent non-achto gear which can be bought from the Armoursmith in Mazcab.
    • Tier 4 luck like the Luck of the Dwarves ring enhances the drop rate.
    • Achto Teralith cuirass can be forced to drop by owning all achto pieces except this one.
      • If an Achto Teralith helmet is owned it must be dropped or converted to coins before looting. Otherwise, a random achto piece might be obtained.

m.post:
Crystal shapeshifters in the Sunken pyramid will always spawn in their melee state, they can still change style based on your weakness or protection/deflect prayers, praying Soul Split and wearing hybrid (crystal) with one piece of ranged armour means they will always stay melee. Crystal shapeshifters will stay aggressive forever as long as the option to make them has been toggled at Angof in Tarddiad and they have a very long aggression range, this makes them very easy to stack up by standing in a corner in the Sunken Pyramid's small room. Legacy Mode and Blood Burst/Barrage spells makes it very easy to both kill them fast and outheal their damage.

Inventory setup

Inventory: Potion reservoir ×4, Ancient elven ritual shard, Enhanced Excalibur, Overload flask (6), Magic notepaper ×500, Overload flask (6), Overload flask (6), Overload flask (6), XP Capacitor 5000 (charging), XP Capacitor 5000 (inactive), Sailfish, Sailfish, Spring cleaner 9001, Slayer Codex

Inventory: Binding contract (ripper demon), Binding contract (ripper demon), Potion reservoir (inactive) ×4, Potion reservoir, Powder of penance ×6, Lantadyme incense sticks ×24, Elder overload potion (6), Elder overload potion (6), XP Capacitor 5000 (charging), XP Capacitor 5000 (inactive), XP Capacitor 5000 (inactive), Elder overload potion (6), Super restore flask (6), Weapon poison+++ flask (6), Weapon poison+++ flask (6), Weapon poison+++ flask (6), Tarddian crystal ×1, Grimy dwarf weed (noted), Grimy lantadyme (noted), Grimy toadflax (noted), Grimy kwuarm (noted), Magic logs (noted), Battlestaff (noted), Grimy irit (noted), Potato cactus (noted), elder seed ×1, Spring cleaner 9001, Slayer Codex

Leave adamantite stone spirits until you've finished drinking a potion to free up an inventory spot.

Make sure your active potion reservoir has at least 5 doses in it. If it does not take an extra overload potion, but you will have to leave the elder seed drops until a space in your inventory is freed up.

To make things easier you should bring the stackable drops as in the inventory setup. They're arranged in order of expected value per hour, so if you get a valuable drop from the rare drop table and need to drop a stack drop the one furthest along.

You should summon a ripper demon before withdrawing your setup

This setup allows 3 hour runs (the length of time for your scripture of Wen to need recharging). You should summon a ripper demon before withdrawing your setup so that you have 3 ripper demons over the run (over 3 hours). On very rare occasions (once every ~10 hours) when not using any auras due to RNG you will take too little damage and you will run out of prayer. You should live for around two minutes when this happens before you need to re-enable your prayers so you should notice when looting which needs to be done every two minutes. Do not replace the armadyl chainskirt with higher armour ranged armour, as you will never die when your prayer is up hence you want to take as much damage as possible both for penance procs and berserkers fury, and in addition armadyl chainskirt has a prayer bonus.

Do not stand in the corner that all other guides online suggest for some reason, stand in front of the statue in the middle of the room. This will add 30 to your kills per hour and drastically reduce your chances of prayer running out and dying (if you stand in the corner as other guides suggest your prayer will run out multiple times per hour, rendering this method not afkable).

If using affliction you will need to use penance aspect not powder of penance as the drain rate is too high for powder.

Suggested perks

Precise 6 and Eruptive 4 are used as cheap perks that can still speed up kills per hour by over 15%. Biting 3 is also relatively easy to get and increases damage noticeably. Lastly, Scavenging 3 is used to indirectly increase profits from the large amounts of free components.

Ruthless 3 gives a constant 7.5% damage boost due to high kill rates, and comboes very easily with Eruptive 4 for additional damage. Biting 4 is used as the best damage boosting armour perk when taking AoE damage into account. Lastly, Scavenging 4 (ideally alone, since Looting clutters up the loot drops) gives lots of free components.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 75 kills per hour running 1 hour trips with fast respawn rate. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

The Bandos armour dropped by General Graardor and his minions is useful, non-degradable, T70 melee power armour. This armour is generally used by lower levelled players and those training Invention. In addition to the armour, Graardor can drop the Bandos hilt, and he and his minions can drop the shards to the godsword blade. Beyond his unique drops, Graardor has decent normal drops consisting of various rune salvage, super restores, ourg bones and more.

Like the other bosses in the dungeon, reaching Graardor requires slaying 40 Bandosian minions. This can take up to 5 minutes by killing goblins, hobgoblins, and jogres just outside the door to the inner stronghold. For short trips, getting the required killcount will cut significantly into the profit per hour. Lasting as long as possible in the boss room will reduce the percentage of time spent killing foot soldiers. Once you have obtained your killcount, you can enter the boss room. There is an intermediate room which is safe from all combat before the boss room itself. Low levelled players should use the main rooms so they can find their perfect respawn ratio as they will take significantly longer to defeat him. High levelled and well-equipped players should use the instance instead; although costing 200,000 gp an hour (150,000 gp with the instance reduction perk from Soul Reaper) an hour, at fastest spawn rate, Graardor will respawn 25 seconds after dying and will drastically increase kill and profit rates.

Those with a Bandosian soulstone, omni soulstone, or an active Totem of Intimidation can skip part or all of the killcount required to face the boss.

Magic or melee should be used; Graardor has a lower affinity towards ranged attacks, thus lowering the chance to land a successful hit dramatically.

Combat with General Graardor is fairly straight forward as there is nothing particularly special about his technique. He has two attacks: a powerful melee attack and a ranged attack. His melee attack is fairly inaccurate with high level armour, and any damage can be offset by using Soul Split; however, a series of good hits by Graardor can be devastating, so it is always good to have high healing food as a security measure. His ranged attack will hit everyone in the room, but deals much less damage than his melee attacks. Overloads are a must, without them, Graardor's attacks will be significantly more accurate, potentially dealing large amounts of damage. Turmoil is highly recommended, and should be used if it is available. General Graardor's bodyguards each attack with a different side of the combat triangle: Sergeant Steelwill uses magic; Grimspike ranged; and Strongstack melee. Grimspike and Strongstack's attack will usually not be a problem. Steelwill poses a small threat as his attacks will hit fairly accurately through melee armour; however, he usually does not do enough damage to worry about. If you so choose, you can stand on the northern wall of the boss room before Graardor respawns. This way, Steelwill will not spot you for some time (perhaps even the entire fight), allowing you to avoid damage from him while he is wandering around.

Graardor himself can be taken down very easily; despite his high damage outputs, he has the lowest health out of all the generals at 40,000 life points. High levelled weapons such as dual drygores or the Inquisitor staff can easily kill him within 15-20 seconds. This kill speed can be increased even further with damage-boosting abilities such as Berserk or Sunshine, but players using Berserk should be extremely careful as Graardor's punches can become extremely damaging, dealing up to 4500 damage and potentially killing the player. If using magic, Sunshine will increase the player's damage as well as deal a small amount of area of effect damage (if Planted Feet is not being used).

Once Graardor has died, kill the minions. It is recommended to kill Steelwill first, as he does the most damage. Kill Strongstack and Grimspike in any order afterwards. If your overload has worn off immediately after the fight with Graardor, kill the minions unboosted. After the fight, you can either use Regenerate to recover lost health with excess adrenaline, utilise Adrenaline stalling to make the next kill quicker and easier, or make use of the Persistant Rage relic. If owned, you can activate elite Enhanced Excalibur instead or use the Guthix's Blessing ultimate ability to recover lost health. Make use of any food dropped by the minions. They can drop 2 sharks or 3 chilli potatoes. They also drop kebabs occasionally, which can come with any other drop the minions give. Avoid drinking overloads and prayer renewals until the moment the boss has respawned.

Bandos armour from General Graardor is 1/384 for a specific unique drop, giving a 1/64 chance for any armour piece. The bandos hilt is a 1/512 drop rate. Shards are 1/768 for a specific shard, giving a 1/256 drop rate for any shard. General Graardor's 3 bodyguards also have the potential to drop pieces of bandos armour (at a much rarer 1/8192 chance for a piece) and shards of the godsword blade. They do not drop the hilt. General Graardor's bones can be banked with your pack yak scroll special or noted using magic notepaper. Rune salvage can be high-alchemised either with an explorer's ring 4 or the spell (if you brought runes), disassembled or sent to your bank as well. It may be worth examining a drop before you alch it as the Grand Exchange price and the High Alch value may differ. Magic logs, limpwurt root, and grimy snapdragons are all dropped noted. Graardor rarely drops coins in amounts around 20,000.
